themeDescription: The unknown, the ancient, and the fascinating

days.title: How Leaves Feed the World
days.learning_objective: Wind power uses moving air to generate electricity.
learning_objectives: Explain how wind turbines convert wind energy into electrical energy.
Identify the benefits and drawbacks of wind power as a renewable energy source.
Design and build a simple model of a wind turbine.
Describe the environmental impact of wind energy generation compared to fossil fuels.

days.title: Energy From Falling Water
days.learning_objective: Water power harnesses flowing water for energy.
learning_objectives: Define water power and its relationship to kinetic energy.
Explain how a hydroelectric dam generates electricity.
Identify the advantages and disadvantages of water power as a renewable energy source.

days.title: Ancient Sunlight Stored
days.learning_objective: Climate is the long-term pattern of weather in a region.
learning_objectives: Define climate and differentiate it from weather.
Identify the major factors influencing climate.
Explain the impact of climate change on the environment.

days.title: Power From Splitting Atoms
days.learning_objective: Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere.
learning_objectives: Identify and describe different types of weather conditions (sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy).
Explain the basic components of weather, including temperature, precipitation, wind, and clouds.
Understand the water cycle and its role in weather patterns.

days.title: Using Less Power
days.learning_objective: Temperature measures how hot or cold something is.
learning_objectives: Define temperature as a measure of how hot or cold something is.
Identify different units of temperature measurement (Celsius, Fahrenheit).
Explain how a thermometer works to measure temperature.
Recognize real-world examples of temperature's impact on daily life.

days.title: Making Less Trash
days.learning_objective: Humidity measures water vapor in the air.
learning_objectives: Define humidity and differentiate between relative and absolute humidity.
Explain how temperature affects humidity levels.
Describe the impact of humidity on weather patterns and human comfort.

days.title: Using Things Again
days.learning_objective: Air pressure is the weight of air pushing on surfaces.
learning_objectives: Define air pressure and explain its effects.
Identify real-world examples of air pressure.
Conduct a simple experiment to demonstrate air pressure.
Explain how changes in air pressure affect weather.

days.title: Turning Old Into New
days.learning_objective: Goals give direction and purpose to our efforts.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define what a goal is and explain its importance.
Students will be able to identify and articulate at least three personal goals.
Students will be able to create a simple action plan to achieve one of their goals.

days.title: Food Becoming Soil
days.learning_objective: Dreams inspire us to imagine better futures.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define and explain the different stages of sleep and their connection to dreaming.
Students will be able to identify common dream symbols and interpret their potential meanings.
Students will be able to articulate how dreams can inspire creative thinking and problem-solving.

days.title: Deciding What You Want
days.learning_objective: Hope sustains us through difficult times.
learning_objectives: Define hope and differentiate it from optimism and wishful thinking.
Identify personal sources of hope and strategies for cultivating them.
Analyze the role of hope in overcoming adversity and achieving goals.

days.title: Things You Do Without Thinking
days.learning_objective: Determination pushes us to overcome obstacles.
learning_objectives: Define determination and explain its importance.
Identify personal obstacles and develop strategies to overcome them.
Apply determination in everyday situations to achieve goals.

days.title: Getting Better on Purpose
days.learning_objective: Practice improves skills through repetition.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define 'practice' and explain its importance.
Students will be able to identify effective practice strategies.
Students will be able to apply practice to improve a skill of their choice.

days.title: When Practice Becomes Skill
days.learning_objective: Learning changes us through new knowledge and experience.
learning_objectives: Identify and describe at least three different learning styles.
Explain the neuroscience behind how the brain processes new information.
Apply effective learning strategies to improve comprehension and retention of information.

days.title: Learning From Getting It Wrong
days.learning_objective: Mistakes are opportunities to learn and grow.
learning_objectives: Define 'mistake' and identify different types of mistakes.
Explain why mistakes are essential for learning and growth.
Develop strategies for analyzing mistakes and extracting valuable lessons.

days.title: Information That Helps You Improve
days.learning_objective: Feedback helps us improve by showing what works.
learning_objectives: Define feedback and explain its importance in personal growth.
Identify different types of feedback and their effectiveness.
Practice giving constructive and specific feedback to peers.
Develop strategies for receiving feedback gracefully and using it for improvement.
Analyze real-world examples of effective and ineffective feedback.

days.title: Getting a Little Better Every Day
days.learning_objective: Mentors guide us with their experience and wisdom.
learning_objectives: Define the role and importance of mentors.
Identify potential mentors in their lives and communities.
Develop strategies for connecting with and learning from mentors.

days.title: Knowing a Lot About Something
days.learning_objective: Teaching shares knowledge and helps others grow.
learning_objectives: Identify key elements of effective teaching strategies.
Develop a basic lesson plan incorporating diverse learning styles.
Demonstrate communication techniques to explain complex topics clearly.

days.title: Knowing What Not to Do
days.learning_objective: Observation gathers information through careful attention.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define observation and differentiate it from simply looking.
Students will be able to identify and utilize different senses in observation activities.
Students will be able to record and interpret observations in a systematic way.

days.title: Different Ways of Being Smart
days.learning_objective: Experimentation tests ideas through controlled trials.
learning_objectives: Define experimentation and its importance in scientific discovery.
Design a controlled experiment with a clear hypothesis, independent variable, and dependent variable.
Collect, analyze, and interpret data from an experiment to draw conclusions.
Identify potential sources of error and bias in experimental design.

days.title: Natural Abilities and Practice
days.learning_objective: Hypothesis is an educated guess that can be tested.
learning_objectives: Define the term 'hypothesis' and explain its purpose in the scientific method.
Formulate a testable hypothesis based on observations and prior knowledge.
Design a simple experiment to test a given hypothesis, identifying independent and dependent variables.

days.title: How We Know What's True
days.learning_objective: Evidence supports conclusions with facts and data.
learning_objectives: Define evidence and differentiate it from opinion.
Identify different types of evidence (e.g., anecdotal, statistical, expert testimony).
Evaluate the credibility and relevance of evidence.
Construct a logical argument supported by evidence.
Apply evidence to solve problems and make informed decisions.

days.title: Guesses You Can Test
days.learning_objective: Reasoning uses logic to draw conclusions from information.
learning_objectives: Identify different types of reasoning (inductive, deductive, abductive).
Distinguish between valid and invalid arguments.
Apply reasoning skills to solve real-world problems and scenarios.

days.title: Asking Nature Questions
days.learning_objective: Inference reaches conclusions based on evidence and reasoning.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define inference in their own words.
Students will be able to identify clues within a text that support an inference.
Students will be able to make a reasonable inference based on provided evidence.

days.title: Seeing on Purpose
days.learning_objective: Comparison identifies similarities and differences.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to identify at least three similarities between two given objects or concepts.
Students will be able to identify at least three differences between two given objects or concepts.
Students will be able to articulate how comparison helps in making informed decisions.

days.title: What the Evidence Means
days.learning_objective: Classification organizes things into categories.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define classification and its purpose.
Students will be able to sort objects based on shared characteristics.
Students will be able to create simple classification systems.

days.title: Explanations That Keep Working
days.learning_objective: Measurement quantifies properties using standard units.
learning_objectives: Identify and differentiate between various units of measurement (length, weight, volume, time).
Apply appropriate tools and techniques to accurately measure objects and substances.
Convert between different units within the same system of measurement (e.g., inches to feet).
Estimate measurements and assess the reasonableness of results.
Explain the importance of standardized units in various contexts.

days.title: Rules Nature Always Follows
days.learning_objective: Estimation makes reasonable guesses about quantities.
learning_objectives: Learners will be able to define estimation and explain its purpose.
Learners will be able to use visual cues to make reasonable estimates.
Learners will be able to apply estimation skills to solve real-world problems.

days.title: How Likely Things Are
days.learning_objective: Hygiene practices prevent disease and promote health.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three important hygiene practices.
Explain how germs spread and cause illness.
Demonstrate proper handwashing technique.
Describe the importance of oral hygiene.

days.title: Finding Patterns in Numbers
days.learning_objective: Nutrition provides the body with necessary nutrients.
learning_objectives: Identify the six major nutrient groups and their primary functions.
Explain the importance of a balanced diet for optimal health.
Distinguish between healthy and unhealthy food choices.

days.title: Why Moving Matters
days.learning_objective: Exercise strengthens the body and improves health.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to define exercise and identify its benefits.
Students will be able to name at least three different types of exercise.
Students will be able to create a simple daily exercise plan.

days.title: Building Stronger Muscles
days.learning_objective: Sleep allows the body and mind to rest and repair.
learning_objectives: Students will be able to explain why sleep is important for physical and mental health.
Students will be able to identify at least three strategies for improving sleep quality.
Students will be able to debunk common misconceptions about sleep duration and habits.
